chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and others, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
From the obligatory causes of Allah's forgiveness, Blessed and Exalted is, feeding of food.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of feeding food according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise tradition from Imam al-Rida (AS), classifying the provision of food as a 'mujjib'—an effective cause or determinant—that actively secures divine forgiveness. This highlights the Shia emphasis on practical charity (sadaqah) not merely as social welfare, but as a spiritual mechanism for cleansing sins and attaining Allah's mercy.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, and someone else from Musa Bin Bakr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘From the Obligatory Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High is feeding of the food’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Afi ibn al-Hakam and others from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Serving food is one of the reasons for which Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, grants forgiveness.”’
